summary:
The Safer Response Act of 2025 (H.R. 4079) amends Section 546 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 290ee-1), which authorizes grants for first responder training relating to the administration of drugs and devices used to reverse overdoses. The bill's principal purpose is to reauthorize and expand the scope of that grant program.

The operative amendments are as follows:

First, in subsection (a), the bill makes a conforming capitalization change, striking "tribes and tribal" and inserting "Tribes and Tribal."

Second, throughout subsections (a), (c), and (d), the bill broadens the category of covered products by striking "approved or cleared" wherever it appears and inserting "approved, cleared, or otherwise legally marketed"—thereby encompassing products lawfully marketed through pathways other than FDA approval or clearance. In the same subsections, it strikes the term "opioid" each place it appears, expanding the program beyond opioid-specific overdoses.

Third, subsection (f) is amended in parallel fashion. The "approved, cleared, or otherwise legally marketed" language is substituted for "approved or cleared" wherever it appears. In paragraph (1), "opioid" is struck. In paragraph (2), "opioid and heroin" is replaced with "opioid, heroin, and other drug," and "opioid overdose" is replaced with "overdose." In paragraph (3), "opioid and heroin" is struck. Collectively, these revisions extend the training and grant purposes to overdoses involving drugs beyond opioids and heroin.

Fourth, subsection (h) revises the authorization of appropriations. The bill strikes the prior authorization of "$36,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023" and inserts "$57,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030." This constitutes an increased authorization of appropriations for a new five-fiscal-year period; it is an authorization only and does not itself appropriate funds.

The bill contains no separate effective-date provision, severability clause, conditions precedent, or sunset provision beyond the temporal limitation inherent in the fiscal-year authorization. The measure was introduced June 23, 2025, by Mr. Harder of California and Mr. Lawler, and referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
